```powershell
$srcCandidate = Join-Path $workspace 'SubFolder\TargetDir'

```

## Step 2 — Resolve the Source and Verify It Is Inside the Workspace

```powershell
$src = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $srcCandidate -ErrorAction Stop).Path
if (-not ($src.StartsWith($workspace + [IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar) -or $src -eq $workspace)) {
    throw "Source '$src' is outside workspace '$workspace'. Aborting."
}
if ($src -eq $workspace) { throw "Refusing to move the workspace root itself." }
```
Fail closed: if the source cannot be resolved, or resolves outside the workspace (e.g., via a symlink or `..`), abort before any mutation.

## Step 3 — Resolve the Destination Parent and Verify Containment

```powershell
$dstParent = Split-Path -Parent $dstCandidate
$dstParentResolved = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $dstParent -ErrorAction Stop).Path
if (-not $dstParentResolved.StartsWith($workspace + [IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar)) {
    throw "Destination parent '$dstParentResolved' is outside workspace. Aborting."
}
$dst = Join-Path $dstParentResolved (Split-Path -Leaf $srcCandidate)
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dst) { throw "Destination '$dst' already exists. Aborting." }
```
The destination's parent must already exist and be inside the workspace; refuse to overwrite an existing destination so unrelated files are never clobbered.

```powershell
if ($dst.StartsWith($src + [IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar)) { throw "Destination is inside source. Aborting." }
```
Confirm the source is a directory and that the move is not nesting a directory into itself. Any failed check throws, and because `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, the script halts before `Move-Item` ever runs.

## Step 5 — Perform the Move Atomically with Literal Paths

```powershell
Write-Host "Moved '$src' -> '$dst'"
```


## Step 2 — Verify Both Paths Are Contained Within the Workspace
```powershell
$wsFull = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($workspace + [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar)
if (-not ([System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($srcPath).StartsWith($wsFull, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase))) {
    throw "Source path escapes workspace: $srcPath"

$destParent = Split-Path -Parent $destPath

    throw "Destination path escapes workspace: $destPath"

```

```powershell
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath) { throw "Destination already exists: $destPath" }

```
Refuse to overwrite an existing destination, confirm the source is a directory, and create only the destination's parent folder — never touching unrelated files or directories.

```powershell

```

```powershell
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $srcPath) { throw "Source still exists after move." }
Write-Host "Moved '$srcPath' -> '$destPath' successfully."
```

```powershell
$workspace = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath "C:\Work\MyWorkspace" -ErrorAction Stop
```
Resolve the workspace root first and fail immediately (`-ErrorAction Stop`) if it doesn't exist. This establishes the trusted boundary all later checks compare against.

## Step 2 — Resolve the Source Path and Verify It's Inside the Workspace
```powershell
$source = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath "C:\Work\MyWorkspace\subdir\MyFolder" -ErrorAction Stop
if (-not ($source.Path.StartsWith($workspace.Path + '\'))) {
    throw "Source path escapes workspace: $($source.Path)"
}
```
`Resolve-Path` normalizes the path (resolving symlinks/relative segments). The prefix check guarantees the source is genuinely inside the workspace — fail closed if not.

## Step 3 — Resolve the Destination Parent and Verify It's Inside the Workspace
```powershell
$destParent = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath "C:\Work\MyWorkspace\archive" -ErrorAction Stop
$dest = Join-Path $destParent.Path (Split-Path $source.Path -Leaf)
if (-not ($destParent.Path.StartsWith($workspace.Path + '\'))) {
    throw "Destination escapes workspace: $($destParent.Path)"
}
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest) {
    throw "Destination already exists: $dest"
}
```
Verify the destination parent is inside the workspace and that the target name doesn't already exist — refusing to overwrite protects unrelated files.

## Step 4 — Pre-Flight Safety Checks
```powershell
if ($source.Path -eq $dest) { throw "Source and destination are identical" }
if ($dest.StartsWith($source.Path + '\')) { throw "Cannot move a directory into itself" }
```
Reject degenerate cases (self-move, moving a folder into its own subtree) before any mutation occurs.

## Step 5 — Execute the Move with LiteralPath
```powershell
Move-Item -LiteralPath $source.Path -Destination $dest -ErrorAction Stop
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest)) { throw "Move verification failed" }
```
`-LiteralPath` ensures special characters (`[`, `]`, wildcards) in names are treated literally. `-ErrorAction Stop` aborts on any failure, and the post-move `Test-Path` verifies success. Because the move is a single atomic operation on the named directory, all unrelated files in the workspace are untouched.
